page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / Stepping aside
title: Stepping aside
topic: Language related to getting the sack
description:
The team from Tip Top Trading has been having a smashing time at the launch of its plastic aubergine. Tom threw one at Dave from the IT department, but it missed him and went through a window! It's time for Paul to hand out some harsh words but he's about to hear some words he won't like. What will Mr Socrates think of it all?
This episode focuses on the language that you might hear to do with people losing their job – or getting the sack.
phrases: I've been doing a strategic review of the company.
I need you to step aside.
The company needs new direction and more dynamic leadership.

listening_challenge.question: Who do you think sent Anna the flowers?
listening_challenge.answer: A secret admirer, so we don't know yet!

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Hello again and welcome back to English at Work. Last time we heard the team from Tip Top Trading having a smashing time at the launch of its plastic aubergine. Tom threw one at Dave from the IT department, but it missed him and went through a window!  It's time for Paul to hand out some harsh words.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: That behaviour just isn't on.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Sorry Paul… but it was quite funny wasn't it?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: No it wasn't.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Sorry Paul, Tom was just angry with Dave. I thought he liked me but we saw him with Julie from accounts.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Really? He seemed such a decent chap… anyway, don't do it again. OK? In the meantime, you're going to have to pay for that broken window.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: What… hey? Bbbut…

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Now, excuse me, I need to take this. Hello, Paul Smith speaking. Ah, Mr Socrates… yes… ah, you've heard…

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Crikey, come on we'd better go.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: That was a good shot Tom! Looks like it's made an impact on Dave. Look, he's sent Anna some flowers.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh there's a note on it. It says "You can count on me" but no name.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: That is a strange thing for him to write.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Hmm, it is and it's not his handwriting.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Maybe a secret admirer eh? I wonder who it could be?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: Are you OK Paul? You look as white as a sheet.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: I'm not actually. Mr Socrates says he's having a strategic review.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: A what?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: He means he's been looking at how the business is operating and how it should operate in the future.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: That sounds serious.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: And as part of his review, he says he wants to downsize and he's asked me to… step aside.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Why? What are you in the way of?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: No Anna. To step aside is a polite way of saying to leave your position in the company.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh. I don't understand Paul. Why?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: He says the company needs new direction and more dynamic leadership.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Crumbs Paul, you can't get more dynamic than you!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Tom! But Paul, you've been a great boss.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Thanks Anna. I guess it's the economic climate, we're not making enough money so cutting staff is inevitable.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Yeah but you cut Denise's job.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Yes but we had to get her back because she was necessary for the smooth running of the department.

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: That's right.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: But Mr Socrates says I'm 'surplus to requirement'.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh, that doesn't sound good… does it?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: If Paul's job is 'surplus to requirement', it means his input to the business is no longer needed. So it's not good news.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Anyway Anna, Mr Socrates wants to know if you got his special message?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Special message? The flowers!?

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: That's strange. Why is Mr Socrates sending you flowers?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: It is a bit strange. Anyway, Paul's news has come as a shock for everyone. Here are some of the phrases Mr Socrates used to break the bad news:
I've been doing a strategic review of the company.
I need to downsize.
I need you to step aside.
The company needs a new direction and more dynamic leadership.
You are surplus to requirement.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Right, I'm going to have to call Mr Socrates and find out why he's sent me flowers.

transcript.speaker: Mr Socrates
transcript.text: Socrates… who wants me?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Erm… hello Mr Socrates… it's Anna here.

transcript.speaker: Mr Socrates
transcript.text: Anna! My favourite girl. Please call me Brad. So glad you called.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I needed to speak to you about the flowers you sent me. I'm very flattered but I don't think…

transcript.speaker: Mr Socrates
transcript.text: The flowers?! Sorry honey, I haven't sent you any flowers but I have sent you an email – have you read it yet?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: No. What did it say?

transcript.speaker: Mr Socrates
transcript.text: I was saying that as I'm giving Paul the chop, would you like a promotion?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: A promotion?

transcript.speaker: Mr Socrates
transcript.text: Yes. You have been an outstanding member of the team so how would you like to be the new manager of Tip Top Trading's London office?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: What a fantastic opportunity and one that Anna surely can't refuse – or can she? And who did send Anna those flowers with a message saying "You can count on me"? Find out what her answer is in the next English at Work. Bye.
